context: The prompt requests merging 'Expanded Security' category into 'Security & IAM' (to be renamed 'Security') in the technical design schema. This involves consolidating duplicate/similar questions, updating IDs, and removing the ExpandedSecurity category. Several decisions need to be made about how to handle overlapping questions and preserve existing data.

questions.question-text: How should overlapping questions between 'Security & IAM' and 'Expanded Security' be handled?

options.label: Keep Security & IAM versions and discard Expanded Security versions
options.pros: Simpler migration, maintains existing answered data in Security & IAM section, clear ownership
options.cons: May lose more detailed options from Expanded Security, requires manual review to ensure no valuable content is lost

options.label: Keep Expanded Security versions and discard Security & IAM versions
options.pros: Expanded Security appears more comprehensive with detailed options, better coverage of security topics
options.cons: Breaks existing answered data, more disruptive migration, Security & IAM section was likely designed earlier

options.label: Merge options from both, creating comprehensive unified questions
options.pros: Preserves all valuable content, most comprehensive coverage, no data loss
options.cons: More complex implementation, requires careful deduplication, may create overly long option lists

questions.recommendation-rationale: Merging provides the most value to users by combining the best aspects of both sections. While more complex to implement, it ensures no valuable security guidance is lost and creates a definitive security questionnaire. This aligns with the goal of creating a comprehensive unified Security category.

questions.question-text: What should happen to existing answered questions in technical-design.json that reference Expanded Security question IDs?

options.label: Automatically migrate to new Security question IDs with best-match mapping
options.pros: Preserves user data automatically, seamless user experience, no manual intervention needed
options.cons: Requires careful mapping logic, risk of incorrect automatic mappings, may need fallback handling

options.label: Clear Expanded Security answers and require users to re-answer in new Security section
options.pros: Simple implementation, no risk of data corruption, users verify all security answers are current
options.cons: Users lose their previous work, frustrating experience, may delay completion of technical design

options.label: Mark Expanded Security answers as 'deprecated' but preserve them for reference during re-answering
options.pros: Users can see previous answers, smooth migration experience, no data loss, allows verification
options.cons: More complex implementation, requires temporary state handling, users must manually re-enter answers

questions.recommendation-rationale: Automatic migration provides the best user experience by preserving their work. A well-designed mapping between old and new question IDs can be validated during implementation. The migration script can log mappings for review and provide a rollback mechanism if issues are detected.

user-selection.value: Do nothing - still no answers provided

questions.question-text: How should the new unified Security question IDs be structured?

options.label: Keep existing SEC_ prefix from Security & IAM, append new questions with incremental numbers
options.pros: Maintains consistency with current IDs, minimal disruption to existing data, clear evolution path
options.cons: May create gaps in numbering if Expanded Security had different structure, less organized

options.label: Renumber all questions sequentially starting from SEC_01, SEC_02, etc.
options.pros: Clean, organized structure, easier to maintain, logical grouping possible
options.cons: Breaks all existing question ID references, requires comprehensive migration of answered data

options.label: Use topic-based prefixes within Security (e.g., SEC_AUTH_, SEC_ENC_, SEC_VULN_)
options.pros: Self-documenting IDs, easier to locate related questions, better organization for large category
options.cons: More complex ID scheme, requires defining topic groupings, longer IDs

questions.recommendation-rationale: Keeping the SEC_ prefix with incremental numbers provides the best balance between simplicity and backward compatibility. Since Security & IAM already exists with this pattern, extending it is the path of least resistance. Topic-based prefixes (option C) could be considered for future enhancements if the category grows significantly.

questions.question-text: Should the unified Security category be organized into sub-groups for better navigation?

options.label: Keep flat structure with all questions in one list
options.pros: Simple implementation, no organizational overhead, easier to search across all questions
options.cons: May be overwhelming if many questions, harder to navigate to specific topics, less intuitive

options.label: Create logical sub-groups (e.g., Identity & Access, Encryption, Scanning, Hardening)
options.pros: Better organization, easier navigation, matches mental model of security domains, improves usability
options.cons: Requires defining group structure, more complex schema, may need to update UI rendering

options.label: Use collapsible sections that can be expanded/collapsed individually
options.pros: Flexible navigation, users can focus on relevant sections, reduces visual clutter
options.cons: Depends on UI capabilities, requires state management for expand/collapse, may hide content

questions.recommendation-rationale: Given that the combined Security category will have many questions (Security & IAM has ~15 questions, Expanded Security has ~20+), organizing them into logical sub-groups will significantly improve usability. This aligns with the prompt requirement to 'update the id and labels' and makes the UI more maintainable. The groups can be implemented as part of the category structure.

questions.question-text: When should config, convention, and requirements files be updated?

options.label: Update all files atomically in a single operation
options.pros: Ensures consistency across all files, no partial states, all changes applied together
options.cons: More complex transaction handling, harder to debug if something fails, all-or-nothing approach

options.label: Update schema first, then update conventions and requirements in separate steps
options.pros: Easier to test and validate each step, can rollback individual steps, clearer progress tracking
options.cons: Temporary inconsistency between files, requires careful sequencing, more prone to partial states

options.label: Update only the technical-design-schema.json, and update conventions/requirements only if they explicitly reference the removed category
options.pros: Minimal changes, focused scope, less risk of breaking unrelated content
options.cons: May miss implicit dependencies, conventions may become outdated, requirements might reference old structure

questions.recommendation-rationale: Updating in steps provides better control and visibility during implementation. The schema update is the core change, and conventions/requirements can be updated after validating the schema works correctly. This approach allows for testing at each stage and makes it easier to document what changed and why.
